Introduction of the Artists – Riverside Ruggers'
notes: Resa Lent explained the Riverside Ruggers’ are a local group who gather and rug hook together. The rugs displayed in the Council Chamber are an example of the work from various rug hookers. She further explained the process of rug hooking and invited all to join.

items.title: County Council Report - Steve O'Neill, County Councillor Ward 4
notes: County Councillor Steve O’Neill, Ward 4 updated Council regarding the County of Wellington’s Roads Committee consideration of automated speed enforcement in community safety and school zones. He provided an update on the spring leaf pick up, the Elora transfer station upgrades, and the roundabout on County Rd 7 at the intersection known as Jefferson Corner.
In response to questions from Council he explained the evaluation process used to establish community safety zones.
Councillor MacDonald inquired if a link to County of Wellington’s website to reporting speeding on County roads could be investigated.

Delegations
Caroline Baker, MCIP, RPP, Baker Planning Group re: Zoning
notes: Amendment for 950-960 St. David Street North (RZ011-22) Caroline Baker indicated she is presenting to Council on behalf of Groves Hospital Volunteer Association and Reid’s Heritage Homes. She reviewed the proposed redevelopment to be a mixed use development with minor modifications likely to be made to the concept being presented.

She indicated Groves Hospital Volunteer Association would like to rebuild the current store “new to you” on the property with the rear portion developed as a residential development with 112 stacked townhouses.
The concept includes 1.2 parking spaces per dwelling unit, 3.5 stories in height, and blended parking between warehousing and retail required.
She further reviewed the updates as a result of the transportation impact study and comments from MTO while outlining the pedestrian access and accessible dwelling units.

The consultant responded to questions from Council regarding the possibility of incorporating a play structure, bicycle parking and storage and perhaps upgrading the sidewalk to accommodate active transportation as well as consideration of including residential above the commercial space.

items.title: Drinking Water Quality Management System Overview and Request for
notes: Council Endorsement
Report D. Masiero, Manager of Environmental Services

D. Masiero, Manager of Environmental Services provided further information on the DWQMS. He reviewed the approval framework for drinking water systems, the operational plan and the 13 elements that form part of the Township’s DWQMS Policy.
In response to questions from Council, he outlined the process as outlined in the DWQMS in the event negative sampling is received.

items.title: RP #02-23 Compensation Market Review
notes: Report from S. Lloyd-Smith, Manager of Purchasing and Risk Management

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer outlined the report, highlighting the 6 plan takers and 4 responses received. The evaluation team consisted of the CAO, Chief Human Resources Officer and the Payroll Coordinator.

Rashid Hasan, Chief Human Resources Officer outlined the scope of the project to assist in attracting staff to the Township, ensure compliance with pay equity legislation and explained the challenges with the existing job market and total compensation packages.

items.title: Advisory Committee Selection Team
notes: Report from K. O'Kane, Manager of Legislative Services & Municipal Clerk

K. O’Kane, Manager of Legislative Services & Municipal Clerk outlined the recruitment process for advisory committees and outlined the proposed process for selection of advisory committee team members including the composition of the section team and the time commitment.
She indicated if more than two Councillors would like to sit on the selection team, the members will be selected by lottery.
Mayor Watters asked for Council volunteers.
Councillors MacDonald, Jefferson, Evoy, and Wilton indicated an interest in filling the positions on the selection team.
Members were selected by lottery, drawing two names from a bowl.
Councillors Jefferson and Evoy were selected.

items.title: Human Resources Services Agreement - Township of Puslinch
notes: Report from R. Hasan, Chief Human Resources Officer

R. Hasan, Chief Human Resources Officer provided the background of an agreement between the Townships of Centre Wellington and Puslinch to share an employee 50/50 time and cost. As the requirements of both municipalities have changed, staff is proposing a fee for service for a suite of HR services in replacement of the shared position. He further indicated this was one of the areas identified in the County’s shared services review, to develop shared a Human Resources model.

items.title: Trade Tracks Facility Rental Exemption
notes: Report from P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services indicated at a previous meeting Trade Tracks requested the waiving of the facility rental fees. Previous Council’s have not entertained waiving the fees. As an alternative, staff is recommending removing the cost of the space rented that is not planned to be utilized by the event in addition to the 15% discounts offered to large events.

motions.item_title: Report from the Committee of the Whole – March 13, 2023
motions.text: THAT items 1 through 5 and item 7 of the Committee of the Whole report dated March 13, 2023 be approved as follows: 1. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington refer the request for the South Wellington Community Lions for waiving of the rental fee for the Trade Track event to staff for a report. 2. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approve application HZ01/2023 to remove a holding zone symbol and give three readings to the corresponding by-law. (Walser Building) 3. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington receives for information Report No. IS2023-07: Stormwater Management Master Plan – Notice of Municipal Class Environmental Assessment Study Commencement. 4. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington adopt a by-law to restrict the weight of vehicles passing over certain bridges in the Township of Centre Wellington, as outlined in Report IS2023-04. 5. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington endorses the proposed collaboration with BioDiffusion Technologies Inc. for the re- paving of Eighth Line West - Wellington Road 18 to Sideroad 5, as outlined in Report No. IS2023-06: AND THAT Council delegates authority to the Managing Director of Infrastructure Services for authorization of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Township and BioDiffusion Technologies Inc., to define the terms and conditions of the proposed collaboration described in Report No. IS2023-06. 7. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington has no objection to the extension of the proposed extended licensed area at the Grand River Raceway, as outlined in their letter dated February 16, 2023 with respect to the Industry Day event scheduled for Monday, August 7, 2023.
